rows: Several large trees were blown down over New Birthright and the southern part of the county.
Quarter-size hail reported in Miller Grove.
Golf ball-size hail reported on Highway 11 north of Cumby.
Tennis ball-size hail reported in the community of Shirley.

Trees uprooted in the community of Brashear.
Large trees uprooted and fences and sheds damaged. Wind speed estimated from EF Scale; time estimated from radar.

Dozens of trees, large tree limbs, power poles, and power lines were downed across the western half of the county. The roof of a barn was blown off onto State Highway 11, and a tree fell on a house on Cranford Street.

One aircraft was overturned at the Sulphur Springs Municipal Airport and at least four hangars were damaged. One large tree was uprooted and a brick wall was blown down. Substantial roof damage occurred in downtown Sulphur Springs. Numerous trees and power lines were blown down a…

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth conducted a damage survey and found that an EF-1 tornado occurred north of Sulphur Springs. Damage was first noted west of Highway 19, along the northbound part of CR 4761. Trees and a shed were damaged. Along Highway 19 and between CR 3…
Golfball-size hail was reported in Sulphur Springs.
A tree was blown across a road and had to be removed.
A large tree fell across the intersection of Oak Avenue and Beckham Street.

According to a damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service in Shreveport, a downburst occurred along the Hopkins/Wood County line. A significant number of trees were downed in Hopkins County along CR 2408, CR 2407, and CR 2403.

According to a damage survey conducted by the National Weather Service in Shreveport, a downburst occurred along the Hopkins/Wood County line. A significant number of trees were downed in Hopkins County along CR 2408, CR 2407, and CR 2403.
Trees were blown down north of Como.
Numerous trees were blown down in the eastern part of the county.

Numerous homes in the Sandy Ranch area south of Sulphur Springs sustained extensive damage. Roofs were torn off, meter boxes were ripped off homes, and one garage was destroyed. Large trees were also uprooted and power lines were blown down. Additional large trees were also blown…
Trees and powerlines were down across the western and northern portions of the county. Several electrical fires were reported from trees falling onto power lines and blown transformers.
A tree fell on a vehicle at CR 4761 near SH 19. The occupants of the vehicle were not injured.
Trees and large limbs were reported down on State Highway 19 near CR 1116.

In Sulphur Springs, trees and large limbs were down in the 1500 block of East Industrial Drive and along State Highway 154 south of the city. A large tree on South Davis Street was also snapped near the base and fell against a house. Power outages were reported on the south side …
Trees and large limbs were reported down on FM 69 in the Black Oak area south of Como.
Trees and large limbs were reported down near the intersection of CR 4546 and 4544.
Nickel size hail was reported 12 miles south-southeast of Sulphur Springs.
Trees were reported down across southeastern Hopkins County.
Quarter size hail fell on County Road 1116 five miles southwest of Sulphur Springs.

A NWS Storm Survey found evidence of a tornado touchdown approximately 4 miles southwest of Sulphur Springs and tracked approximately 5.5 miles to the northeast. One mobile home was destroyed resulting in two injuries. A pre-fabricated metal building on Highway 19 south of County…
Power poles and large trees were damaged at the intersection of Highway 19 and Highway 154 on the north side of Sulphur Springs.
A roof was caved in, a truck was overturned, and debris was noted on Irwin Rd between Drexel Drive and Hines Drive in Sulphur Springs.

A NWS storm survey found evidence of a tornado in a sub-division 2 miles east of Sulphur Springs. Around 50 homes suffered some degree of roof damage, two of which sustained more severe damage after being impaled by large tree branches. This damage was consistent with the rating …
Two tractor trailers were overturned on Interstate 30 at mile marker 131.

A county commissioner reported approximately 50 trees were over roads in the Precinct 2 area. Most of these trees were broken off at 30 to 40 feet up the tree trunk. It took two days to clean up the tree debris.

Hopkins County local and county Emergency Management officials determined that damage and debris reported near the intersection of Interstate 30 and Highway 67 was caused by straight line winds of approximately 70 mph. Winds damaged trees, powerlines and power poles near this loc…
The automated weather station at the Sulphur Springs Municipal Airport (KSLR) measured a 67 mph wind gust.
Dime size hail was reported on CR 4131, two miles south of Cumby.
Trees were knocked down by thunderstorm winds on CR 4131, two miles south of Cumby.
Quarter size hail was reported on I-30 at mile marker 125 on the southeast side of Sulphur Springs.
Half inch to penny size hail was reported in Pickton.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Sulphur Springs.
Quarter size hail fell in the town of Nelta.
Trees were blown down in the Greenpond area, southwest of Como. Some of these trees were blocking roads.

Several trees were knocked down across the county but the hardest hit area was along Hwy 19 north of Sulphur Springs. On either side of the highway, numerous trees were knocked down and many trees blocked roads. On CR 4769, a carport was blown across the road. The roof of an unoc…
A large tree was blown through power lines by thunderstorm winds on Reservoir St. in Sulphur Springs. A utility pole near Mulberry Street and Middle Street was snapped in two.

Several travel trailers were blown over, many trees and power poles were knocked down, and a metal building was severely damaged in Sulphur Springs. A tree at The Propane Company on Loop 31 was snapped and fell on a carport which damaged the car underneath the covering.
Trees were knocked down on CRs 3511 and 3504. A barn in the area was also destroyed.
Several trees were blown down by estimated 60 MPH winds. One tree fell on a house on CR 3504. Trees were also reported down on CR 3511, and a barn in the area was destroyed.
Winds were estimated to be near 60 mph in Como.
A barn in the Pickton-Pine Forest area lost its metal roof.
Thunderstorm wind speeds were estimated to be around 60 MPH in Como. At least one large tree was snapped in the area.
Thunderstorm wind speeds were estimated to be around 60 MPH in Pickton.

Medium sized trees were knocked down along FM 3236 north-northeast of Sulphur Springs. Some sheds were also displaced several yards along the same road. One residential home on FM 3236 sustained damage. The damage was the result of a microburst from a dissipating, high-based thun…
Thunderstorm winds gusted up to 60 MPH.
Multiple trees were blown down due to high winds about 5 miles south of Cumby.
Powerlines and a large tree blocked a highway about 4 miles southwest of Sulphur Springs.
Approximately 10 moderate sized trees in Sulphur Springs were knocked down by thunderstorm winds. The emergency manager noted that the trees were all already dead or dying.
A very brief tornado touched down in open field near FM 3389 and CR 1170, south of Brashear.

Trained spotters and Sulphur Springs PD reported a tornado near Highway 19 North and Loop 301 on the north side of town. This tornado touched down in open country but did damage to a few power poles, power lines, and trees. The tornado was rated an EF-0 with maximum estimated win…

Trained storm spotters reported a tornado 6 miles northwest of Winnsboro which is also about 2 miles southeast of Pickton. The tornado damaged a few trees. Maximum wind speeds were likely around 80 mph.
Numerous trees were blown down by estimated 65 MPH winds near Farm-to-Market Roads 71 and 69.
Several trees were blown down by estimated winds of 60 MPH south of Como along Highway 69.
Law enforcement reported large trees blown down throughout the city of Sulphur Springs.
Pea to quarter sized hail fell for approximately 20 minutes in Cumby.
Sulphur Springs Municipal Airport (KSLR) measured a 62 MPH thunderstorm wind gust.

A National Weather Service damage survey crew determined a tornado produced EF1 damage in northern Hopkins County, near the city of Birthright. This tornado caused damage to several homes and businesses, including the Birthright Volunteer Fire Department building. A total of 76 h…
Thunderstorms winds blew a tree onto a house and also took the roof off a metal barn.
The Sulphur Springs Municipal airport AWOS (KSLR) measured a 55 knot wind.
Sulphur Springs News reported trees blown down, one of which landed on a parked car. Power lines were also reported blown down county-wide. Several homes also reported roof damage.
A social media report indicated damage to a gas station awning near the Hospital in Sulphur Springs, TX.
A social media report indicated large trees blown down on FM 2653 near Ridgeway, TX.

Amateur radio operators estimated winds between 60 and 70 mph in Sulphur Springs. Several trees were blown over, and numerous carports were damaged. Additionally, the Sulphur Springs airport had several airplanes moved or damaged as a result of the storm.
A social media report indicated that airplanes were displaced at Sulphur Springs Municipal Airport.
A storm chaser observed a brief tornado south of Sulphur Springs at 5:33 PM.
A report was received via amateur radio indicating quarter-sized hail approximately 4 miles south of Sulphur Springs, TX.
A trained spotter reported quarter-sized hail in Como, TX.

Emergency management reported significant damage to very large commercial chicken coop structures. Two were completely destroyed and one partially destroyed, and a very large number of chickens were killed.

Broadcast media reported several trees down south of Sulphur Springs near County Road 1116 and County Road 1174 off of Highway 19.
Trained spotters reported a brief tornado near the intersection of Hopkins County Roads 2393 and 2399. Debris was encountered near the intersection.
Hopkins County Sheriff's Department reported trees down on County Road 3528 near the town of Weaver, TX.
Hopkins County Sheriff's Department reported a 60 MPH wind gust in the city of Miller Grove, or approximately 7 miles south-southeast of the city of Cumby, TX.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail on the south side of the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.

Hopkins County Sheriff's Department reported that wooden rafters were blown off of a barn, small out-buildings were flipped, and a tree with a 12 inch base was uprooted. This occurred in the northwest part of Hopkins County.
Hopkins County Sheriff's Department reported quarter size hail in the community of Brashear, TX.
Emergency management reported golf ball size hail in the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.
Emergency management reported golf ball size hail in the city of Seymore, TX.
Emergency management reported downed power poles and a 20-inch diameter tree toppled near the intersection of CR 1100 and FM 3389 just west of the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.
An amateur radio report indicated golf ball size hail in the city of Como, TX.
An amateur radio report indicated quarter-size hail in the city of Como, TX.
A social media report indicated penny-size hail approximately 7 miles north-northeast of the city of Como, TX.
Cumby Police Department reported quarter size hail in the city of Cumby, TX.
The Sulphur Springs Airport Automated Weather Observation System (AWOS) reported a wind gust of 59 MPH.

Emergency management reported a tree down and blocking the road just west of the community of Peerless along Highway 71. Additional trees were also knocked down in the area, usually isolated in nature, but did block some county roads.
Emergency management reported trees down in the northwestern part of the county, including CRs 4743 and 4744.
Emergency management reported a tree down, and a barn damaged on CR 2408 in the southeast part of the county. Other isolated trees were knocked down in the area, including on CR 2409 and CR 2403.

A social media report indicated a tree being uprooted in the town of Miller Grove, TX, but emergency management reported many trees and tree limbs being knocked down in the western portions of the county.
A homeowner near Cooper Lake reported huge trees broke off and uprooted on their property. The tops of trees were carried quite a ways, and shingles were blown off the roof.
Sulphur Springs Police Department reported quarter size hail near the intersection of FM 1537 and FM 69.
A public report indicated half-dollar size hail approximately 8 miles east-northeast of the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.
Amateur radio reported baseball size hail approximately 6 miles east of the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.
Amateur radio reported tennis ball size hail on Interstate 30 exit 135.
The Sulphur Springs Airport Automated Weather Observation System (AWOS) reported a wind gust of 61 MPH.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage to 2 sheds and several trees near FM 2437 and 2428 in far southern Hopkins County. Several trees lost several 8-14 diameter tree limbs. One shed was collapsed and another was leaning.
A resident sent in a picture of a very large tree branch that broke off in high thunderstorm winds, causing scattered damage around the property including a metal fence and the roof of the home.
A public report indicated dime sized hail in the city of Sulphur Springs, TX.
Law enforcement reported quarter to golf ball sized hail in Cumby, TX.
Law enforcement reported quarter sized hail near the intersection of FM 71 and CR 4749, about 3 miles west of Peerless, TX.
Trees were reported down along FM 900 from Sulphur Bluff to Saltillo. An old barn also suffered some roof damage.
A camper was rolled and destroyed in high thunderstorm winds.
A public report indicated golf ball sized hail in Miller Grove, TX.

According to eyewitness and video the second tornado started in a field west of County Road 1164. It moved northeast striking a home at the intersection of CR 3389 and FM 1567. This home sustained EF2 damage when the winds took the roof and attic off the house. The tornado contin…
A dairy farm on CR 2408 was damaged and several trees were snapped in the same area. Sheets of tin roofing were blown off the buildings on the farm, and a large barn was destroyed.

An EF-1 tornado moved through far southeast Hopkins County, causing the most notable damage in Pickton. Several homes, businesses, and a church were damaged in Pickton. Most of the structural damage was confined to roof damage. All along the track, notable tree damage was observe…
Half dollar size hail was reported near Winnsboro.

A NWS survey team determined a combination of straight line winds and microbursts caused damage in and around the Como area of Hopkins County. Notable damage was first observed west of Como on FM 1567 where two homes sustained minor roof damage and notable tree damage was observe…
Golf ball sized hail reported at FM499 and FM275 in Cumby.
Golf ball sized hail was observed at Highway 19 and CR 1174.
Nickel hail was observed 3 miles south of Sulphur Springs.
Half dollar to ping pong ball sized hail was reported on FM 1537 northeast of Sulphur Springs.
Law enforcement reported 3-inch diameter hail 6 miles north of Como.
Thunderstorm winds damaged several lightweight metal structures on a property in the Pickton area. Large tree branches were also knocked down.
Numerous trees were blown down across the county with several roads blocked. Powerlines were also reported down in some areas.

A 61 mph wind gust was measured at the KSLR AWOS.
Law enforcement reported quarter size hail fell on CR 1157.
Broadcast media produced an image of a tree fallen onto a home in Cumby, causing damage to its roof.
